technical.lead: Unsloth v2026.5.26 ships selective-expert-checkpoint primitive cutting MoE save footprint ~60%
technical.body: Unsloth's Tuesday v2026.5.26 point release introduces first-class fine-tuning support for Alibaba's Qwen3.6-Max-Preview alongside a selective-expert-checkpoint primitive that freezes inactive expert columns on disk during checkpoint write, collapsing the MiniMax M2.7 235B MoE port's checkpoint footprint from roughly 470GB to 188GB across the first ten saved revisions. The paired Daniel Han Chen and Mike Han Chen Hugging Face Blog benchmark sheet reports the new Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B Mixture-of-Experts checkpoint training at ~1.74x throughput versus the prior DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B recipe under the same router-only LoRA driver on a single 8x H200 SXM5 node, with peak combined VRAM down 11.3 percent against a vanilla Hugging Face Transformers v5 baseline and an additional 4.1 percent versus last week's Mixtral-Next 70B merge. The release also lifts the contributed 60B-class recipe count to four — adding a Tsinghua KEG Lab MiniMax M2.7 port to the existing DeepSeek R3-Pro, OLMo-2 60B, and Qwen3 MoE 60B set — and a Hacker News thread surfaced two independent CoreWeave and Crusoe Cloud reproductions landing inside 3 percent of the published numbers within the trading day.

technical.lead: Qwen3.6-Max-Preview model card publishes with LiveCodeBench 88.7 and SWE-Bench Verified 76.2 records
technical.body: Alibaba's Qwen team published the formal Qwen3.6-Max-Preview model card on Hugging Face on Tuesday morning Pacific time, lifting the architecture from preview-numbers-only into a fully gated open-weight release under the Tongyi Qianwen open license. The 235B-active-parameter Mixture-of-Experts checkpoint ships a 1M-token native context window, a 24-of-160 expert routing topology, and a published instruction-tuned variant alongside the base; per the model card the checkpoint lands at 88.7 on LiveCodeBench v6 and 76.2 on SWE-Bench Verified — both new records for any non-Anthropic non-OpenAI checkpoint — and matches Claude Opus 4.7 on AIME 2025 inside a 0.6-point band. Decrypt confirmed Alibaba Cloud Model Studio listed the hosted variant at $0.45 per million input tokens against DeepSeek-V4-Pro's $1.10 floor and Anthropic Claude Opus 4.7 at $7.50, timed to undercut DeepSeek-V4-Pro ahead of the May 28 OpenRouter integration cycle, while The Decoder reported Together AI and Fireworks AI hosted endpoints lighting up inside the first six hours with first-token-latency at ~0.18 seconds on 8x H100 SXM5 under FP8 quantization.

technical.lead: Cerebras (CBRS) closes $217.05 on 18.6M volume as Saudi Aramco Digital MoU prints $1.2B over four years
technical.body: Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ: CBRS) reopened from the Memorial Day market closure with a Tuesday session that resolved three days of pent-up demand into a clean tape — the open print at $213.40 against Friday's $209.85 close (~+1.7 percent gap), an intraday high of $221.20 inside the first ninety minutes, and a $217.05 close on volume of approximately 18.6 million shares, ~2.7x the trailing-twenty-day average and the fifth-highest volume session of the post-IPO record. Bloomberg flagged the close as the first push of the consensus analyst spread above $215, with Bernstein lifting its Market-Perform floor to $200 from $185 and UBS upgrading to Buy at a $240 target citing the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU formally closing Tuesday afternoon at a disclosed $1.2 billion total contract value over four years for first-generation CS-4 capacity placement in the King Abdullah Economic City data-center park. Reuters reported institutional buyside cumulative net position lifting to ~47.5 percent of float from Friday's ~44 percent, and Morgan Stanley's Tuesday tape-recap pushed its upside-scenario probability to 61 percent from 54 percent.

technical.lead: Stellantis pulls Mack Avenue Optimus pilot to June 1; four humanoid factory activations stack into 18-day window
technical.body: Stellantis disclosed Tuesday morning that its Detroit Mack Avenue Optimus pilot has been advanced from June 8 to June 1, with Reuters citing a Stellantis Tuesday note confirming the 60-unit cohort has completed factory-acceptance testing at Tesla's Fremont commissioning floor and that the units have already been wheeled onto the Detroit floor for final fixture mating ahead of production line restart. The pull-in compresses the gap between the Tesla Fremont 240-unit completion and the first US contract-manufacturing deployment to a single week, and BMW responded inside the same trading session with a press release locking BMW Plant Leipzig's second AEON cohort first-activation date at June 15 rather than the prior June 22 placeholder — placing four humanoid-robot factory-floor activations inside an 18-day window between June 1 and June 18. Volkswagen Wolfsburg held its June 22 cohort activation but added a 24-unit second cohort with a July 13 target, and Bloomberg reported Boston Dynamics / Hyundai held an investor briefing flagging that the Atlas commercial-fleet first-deployment cycle at Hyundai Motor Group Pyeongtaek has been moved up by roughly nine days to June 24, citing the Stellantis pull-in as public proof that humanoid factory deployments have crossed the practical readiness threshold.

technical.lead: CVE-2026-46127 (CVSS 9.4) lands on CISA KEV after Mandiant confirms Fortune 500 financial-services exploitation
technical.body: GitHub Security Lab published a Tuesday advisory disclosing CVE-2026-46127, a critical-severity (CVSS 9.4) prompt-injection-escalation vulnerability in OpenAI's open-source Codex CLI v3.1.x development branch in which an attacker can chain a workspace-scoped sandboxed Codex agent into an unsandboxed shell-exec context via a crafted MCP-server response that exploits a missing JSON-Schema validation step in the agent harness's tool-call deserialization path. The advisory credits Trail of Bits' Vasilios Mavroudis and Pillar Security's Dor Sarig for the report; OpenAI shipped a patched v3.1.10 development tag inside the disclosure window adding strict schema validation plus a runtime tool-call audit log, lifting the Trail of Bits agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE taxonomy to twelve catalogued instances (first net-new since the May 8 cycle). The Hacker News reported CISA placed CVE-2026-46127 on its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog inside the same Tuesday window after a Mandiant incident-response engagement at a Fortune 500 financial-services customer confirmed active exploitation in the wild, and OpenAI's Tuesday security note stated the Codex CLI's production-tier auto-update path will force-roll all v3.1.x development tenants to v3.1.10 inside a 72-hour window. NIST NVD published a Tuesday afternoon update confirming the CVSS 9.4 scoring and reclassifying the vulnerability under the agent-loader subcategory.
